reports.summary: Interface versus implementation before porting: host-runtime 535/19402, shm-transport 152/1963, tokenizer 2/38, shm-native 29/1860 (pub items / non-blank non-comment implementation lines outside cfg(test)). host-runtime and shm-native are deep; shm-transport is deep; tokenizer is a two-function facade over the vocabulary table by design. The host runtime has no dependency on the product daemon (zero references), and shm-transport is its only transport adapter. No Strong candidate.

candidates.title: Remove the unused producer half of frame_channel
candidates.interface: `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod frame_channel`: 47 public items, of which connection, dispatch, ring_transport, routing, and runtime use `FrameSender`, `frame_sender`, `InboundFrame`, `OwnedInboundFrame`, `InboundEvent`, `OutboundFrame`, `DirectFrame`, `DirectSerializer`, `QueuedOutboundFrame`, `SenderQueue`, `ReadClose`, `RejectedFrame`, `CopyCounter`
candidates.implementation: the producer half of `frame_channel.rs`: `ProducerError`, `ProducerReservation`, `ProducedBody`, `LeaseTracker`, `LeaseClose`, `ReceiveLease::segmented`, and the matching `frame_channel/contract_tests.rs` cases (about 300 of the module's 616 implementation lines) have no caller outside the module's own contract tests

deletion_test.rationale: Deleting the producer half makes the complexity vanish rather than move: no production or test caller outside `frame_channel` constructs a `ProducerReservation` or a `LeaseTracker`, and the mandatory-ring refactor that removed the TCP channel left them behind.

candidates.rationale: Not Strong: a deletion of dead surface, not a deepening, so the interface metric does not apply. Recorded rather than done in U3 because the wave's rule is no behavior change beyond renames, and the property catalog carries records (`ring-a-segmented-inbound-body-has-no-production-producer` and siblings) that describe this exact dead surface and must be re-dispositioned when it goes.
candidates.follow_up: remove after U3 lands, together with the catalog records that describe the dead surface

candidates.title: Inline the setup-proof wrappers onto the shared transcript
candidates.interface: `host_runtime::auth::compute_proof` and the addon's `setup.rs` proof call, both forwarding every argument to `shm_transport::setup_auth::compute_proof`
candidates.implementation: two nine-line forwarding wrappers plus the test-local `raw_client::proof` oracle, which must stay independent

deletion_test.rationale: Re-exporting the shared function removes the wrappers without moving anything; the oracle in `tests/support/raw_client.rs` is deliberately a separate implementation and is not part of the candidate.

candidates.rationale: Not Strong: pure forwarding removal, no deepening. Recorded; landing it changes public paths the U3 catalogs cite.

candidates.title: Share the filesystem-policy helpers between harness_closure and instance
candidates.interface: `instance::{is_safe_ancestor, owner_uid, mode_bits, hex}` (pub(crate)) and `harness_closure::{verify_safe_ancestor, owner_uid, mode_bits, hex, S_ISVTX}` (private)
candidates.implementation: two copies of the sticky-bit, owner, and mode checks that decide whether a directory ancestor is trusted; the two had already drifted in how they read the mode

deletion_test.rationale: Deleting the private copies and calling `instance`'s concentrates the policy in one module; `harness_closure` already depends on `crate::instance`.

candidates.rationale: Not Strong on the metric: the shared helpers are a handful of lines, so the interface is not materially smaller than the implementation. Recorded; the two copies must be compared line by line before one is deleted because the drift may be intentional for closure roots.
candidates.follow_up: compare the two ancestor policies, then delete the private copy or document why closure roots differ
